iteration_15.purpose: Measure this skill against no skill, and against the pre-compaction version, on a case suite built differently from the `evals` list below.
iteration_15.suite: Eight cases, each current `main` with one merged fix reverted, so the case builds on the active toolchain and the fix diff is the maintainers' own adjudication. This is NOT the `evals` list below; no case is shared with it. One case is current `main` unreverted, as a false-positive control.
iteration_15.isolation: Fresh reviewer context per run, same prompt, same git-free tree. Only the skill arms receive a SKILL.md path. No arm receives an answer key, and the reverted trees carry no history that would reveal the fix.

measures.pass_rate: The report names the reverted defect and gives the right verdict. Graded by regex, not judgement.
measures.findings_filed: How many items the report files. Each seeded case holds exactly one defect, so on a case that passes every further item is noise, and on the false-positive control every item is. This is the precision measure the pass rate cannot see.

result.pre_compaction_skill: pass rate 1.000, 2.25 findings per file, 116,645 tokens, 521 s

iteration_15.what_this_does_not_settle: Every content assertion passes in both the no-skill and skill arms, so the pass rate still measures recall on defects a careful reader finds unaided. The advantage shown here is precision and cost. No case in this suite requires an escalation path, which is the gap the next suite should close.
iteration_15.method_note: Findings filed was added after a batch review of five real pull requests filed fourteen findings of which five were worth acting on, while the pass rate scored 1.000. A suite in which every case has a planted defect rewards recall and charges nothing for a finding that should not have been filed. Report both numbers.
iteration_15.provenance_warning: The pre-compaction arm was run from a scratch worktree 62 commits behind this branch, which is how the discrepancy was found. Check a worktree against the pull request head before quoting any number measured in it.

required_finding_fields: what the witness shows and does not show
report_contract.inline_suggestion_rule: Require a high-confidence exact-line replacement that type-checks or is documentation-only. Do not require or reward a suggestion for an unresolved source reading.
report_contract.publication_boundary: The review is advisory: it must not approve, request changes, merge, label, or mutate a contributor branch.

notes:
Each case reviews a file in this repository, not a fixture, so a case is only valid at a commit where the defect is still present. Runs must review a worktree built from `pinned_commit`, never the working tree. Reviewing the working tree is what retired the 940 case when its fix merged, and 940 was the strongest case in the set.

Selection rule: keep a case only if it separates the arms. Measured in iteration 4, the one iteration where all six cases ran with and without the skill:
  940            9/9 vs 5/9   +0.444
  ClaudesCycles  8/8 vs 6/8   +0.250
  1063           7/7 vs 6/7   +0.143   (dropped after iteration 8; see below)
  PR 4660        8/8 vs 7/8   +0.125
  918            6/6 vs 6/6    0.000
  Green 72       6/6 vs 6/6    0.000
918 and Green 72 were dropped after that run. Neither measured anything across four iterations. Mean gap over the retained four is 0.240, against 0.160 over the original six.

Why those two scored zero is the rule for choosing replacements. A stray `∀ (ω : Ordinal)` binder and a reversed conclusion are both visible by reading the file against its own docstring, and the control reads carefully too. The cases that separate the arms need something outside the file: 940 needs erdosproblems.com, which returns 403 to the control, and ClaudesCycles needs a kernel-checked witness rather than an argument. Before adding a case, ask whether a careful reader with no network and no Lean could reach the answer. If yes it is documentation, not a test.

An expected output is only as good as its check. Four have been overturned by runs: case 3 in iteration 1, case 2 in iteration 3, Green 72 in iteration 4, case 2 again in iteration 7. Every one of those was a key I reasoned out rather than checked. The two cases that have never been overturned are the two whose keys are backed by a Lean proof. Prefer keys a machine settles.

Second rule on keys: prefer a defect whose fix is already merged. A merged fix means the maintainers adjudicated the finding, so the key is theirs and not mine. Better still if someone else found it. Of the original four cases only 940 had a merged fix, and 940 is the only key never overturned and the strongest discriminator at +0.222. The other three were pinned to open or abandoned pull requests, and all three keys had to be revised. Pinning made this rule free, because a merged fix no longer erases its own case.

Case 2 was Erdős 939 through iteration 2, retired for the same reason as 918 and Green 72: the control scored 6 of 6 twice, and the finding is a worked example in references/defect-classes.md, so the runs measured recall rather than procedure. Keep eval targets and the worked examples in that reference disjoint.

Case 4 comes from the unresolved leads in #4896, which are triage notes rather than confirmed defects, and whose author warns they may contain transcription errors. Its expected output is my adjudication of someone else's hypothesis, so a run that produces a witness against it is evidence the case is wrong, not the run.

Iteration 8 re-ran the control against these four cases at their pins. It scored 0.882, against the 0.8396 carried since iteration 4 over a six-case set that no longer exists. The control is stronger than that stale figure implied: it built Lean on case 2 and swept it 8/8, and case 1 rose from 5/9 to 7/9. Case 2 no longer separates the arms at all.

No gap can be computed yet. Every `with_skill` number on record was measured against the working tree, not against a worktree at the pin, so it is not on the same footing as this control. The skill arm has to be re-run at the pins before any delta from this set means anything. Per-case control results are in the `iteration_8` field of each case.

Iteration 8 dropped Erdős 1063. Measured on the same footing both arms scored 8/8, so the gap is 0.000, and the skill arm spent 1.28x the tokens and 2.3x the wall clock to reach it. The control built Lean, machine-checked the comparator collapse and returned the right verdict unaided. Erdős 14 replaces it, pinned before merged #1382.

Iteration 8 is the first like-for-like delta in the exercise: control 0.882, skill 0.969, gap +0.087 over the four cases as run, or +0.116 over the three retained. It cost 142,835 tokens against 89,410 and 1755s against 440s, so 1.6x tokens and 4.0x wall clock. The whole gap sits in two assertions in two cases, source fidelity on 940 and the positive control on ClaudesCycles. Two of the four cases returned 0.000. Every delta quoted before this one compared arms reading different file states and should not be used.

Six cases from iteration 9. Erdős 274 (merged #4164) and Erdős 92 (merged #1525) were added, both found by other people, both on the source-fidelity axis where the control measurably fails. Erdős 128 (merged #4501) was considered and rejected: its class is quantifier scope visible on a read, which is what scored 0.000 on 918. Four of the six now have a merged fix and three were found by someone other than me. Case 4 is the exception on purpose, and its adjudication field says so.

Iteration 9, the finding that matters. Every case carrying an assertion that requires the reviewer to *check* something discriminates: 940 at +0.222 on assertion 9, ClaudesCycles at +0.125 on assertion 7. Every case whose assertions only require reaching the right conclusion scores 0.000: 1063, 265, and now Erdős 92, where both arms took 7/7 while only the skill arm proved f 2 = 1, the falsity of the right-hand side and two negative controls in Lean. The set was measuring whether a reviewer reaches the answer, which the control does well, rather than whether it verifies the answer, which is what the skill claims. A verification assertion has been added to cases 4, 5 and 6.

These additions are retrofitted after seeing the reports, which is a bias. They must not be graded against reports that already exist. Any case carrying an `assertions_added_iteration_9` field needs both arms re-run before its gap is quoted again. The iteration 8 case 4 result is the retrospective check on the idea: the control there could not build and gave only a pen-and-paper construction, while the skill arm proved exploit_reduction sorry-free, so the assertion would have separated them.

Iteration 9 results. The class 4 sweep works: case 4 went 7/8 to 8/8 and the self-answer is now proved by rfl rather than missed. Erdős 274 discriminates at +0.167, on source fidelity, and the control failed it the same way it failed 940, by hitting the 403 and substituting a reconstruction that contradicts the page. Erdős 92 does not discriminate as keyed, 7/7 both arms, which is what prompted the verification assertion added to cases 4, 5 and 6.

Iteration 10. Both arms re-run on the four cases with the verification assertions in place, each arm in its own worktree. Control 0.877, skill 1.000, gap +0.123, at 1.57x tokens and 3.83x wall clock. The skill arm scored 1.000 on every case, so nothing in the current set separates further.

The verification assertions are validated. Erdős 92 went from 0.000 on the seven-assertion key to +0.125 with no change in either arm's behaviour: the iteration 9 skill run had already proved f 2 = 1 in Lean and the key could not see it. Every control failure across all four cases is a verification failure.

Two cases now have paired runs, and they disagree. Erdős 274 gave +0.167 in iteration 9 separating on source fidelity, and +0.143 in iteration 10 separating on verification, because the iteration 9 control hit the 403 and the iteration 10 control did not. Single paired runs cannot distinguish a real gap from run-to-run variance. Repeats are the outstanding work.

Erdős 14 does not discriminate and both arms verified it. The rule is narrower than iteration 9 stated: a verification assertion separates the arms when verifying means constructing something, not when it means printing something.

Iteration 11, repeats. Every control reached n=3 and every skill arm n>=2, nineteen runs in all. Per-case gap against the control mean: 940 +0.148, 14 +0.000, ClaudesCycles +0.125, 265 +0.222, 274 +0.238, 92 +0.125. Mean over the six cases +0.143, against the +0.123 reported from iteration 10's single sweep. The average survived; three of the six components did not.

The skill arm scored 1.000 in all thirteen paired runs, across six cases. That is a hard ceiling, not a near one, so every gap here measures the control and the mean is a floor.

The finding worth keeping: a case measures reliably only when the control's failure is a fixed habit. 265, 92 and 14 reproduce exactly three times each regardless of effort, and the 265 control scored 7/9 whether or not it built Lean. 940, 274 and ClaudesCycles drift, because passing there depends on the run choosing to do work it is always capable of. ClaudesCycles drifted to ceiling and should be retired unless its assertions are made harder.

The rep 3 skill runs were not bought. Thirteen consecutive 1.000s make their information value near zero, and one pair was already dead since the ClaudesCycles control reached ceiling.

evals.prompt: can you check FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/14.lean? the two statements are hard to read and I want to know they say what the problem actually asks
evals.expected_output: NEEDS REVISION, on erdos_14b. It reads `∃ (A : Set ℕ), IsLittleO atTop (nonUniqueSumCount A) squareRoot ↔ answer(sorry)`. The body of an existential extends as far right as it can, so the binder scopes over the iff and the statement means `∃ A, (IsLittleO ... ↔ answer(sorry))`. The source asks whether such an A exists, which is `(∃ A, IsLittleO ...) ↔ answer(sorry)`, with the slot outside the binder. erdos_14a is not a defect: it is wrapped in redundant parentheses and reads badly, but its bracketing is correct, and reporting it as broken is the failure mode this case tests.
evals.adjudication: merged. Found by YaelDillies, not by me, and accepted by the maintainers, so the answer key is not my reasoning. The fix survived later refactoring: on main the declaration is erdos_14.parts.ii and still reads answer(sorry) <-> exists A, ... with the slot outside the binder.
evals.replaces: Erdos 1063, dropped after iteration 8 measured both arms at 8/8 on it.
evals.notes: Chosen against two rules the earlier cases failed. The fix is merged, so the ground truth is the maintainers' rather than mine; of the original four cases only 940 had that, and 940 is the only key never overturned. And the defect's consequence lands where controls demonstrably fail: the bracketing leaves an answer slot on a research open statement that no longer records the source's question, and self-answer detection is the one assertion no control run has ever passed. Discrimination is unmeasured until this case runs. Assertion 6 deliberately stops at what the merged diff settles and does not claim the statement is trivially satisfiable, which I have not checked.

The report says the intended reading puts the answer slot outside the existential, and ties that to what the source asks
The report checks the elaboration rather than asserting the precedence from memory, for instance by elaborating both readings or printing the parsed statement
The report does not report erdos_14a as a defect, or says explicitly that its bracketing is correct despite the redundant parentheses
The report says what the mis-bracketing costs, that the answer slot no longer records the question the source asks

evals.prompt: can you review PR #4660 before I approve it? someone said the tsum has no Summable hypothesis and I want to know if that actually matters
evals.expected_output: NEEDS REVISION, and blocking. IsRationalPairSequence requires `exists q : Q, tsum n, 1/(a n) = q`. In Mathlib tsum of a family that is not Summable is 0, and 0 is rational, so the condition reads 'sums to a rational OR diverges'. The consequence is worse than a loose definition: erdos_265 itself becomes provable. Its growth condition GrowthExceedsOne is exists-frequently, `exists-freq n, c^(2^n) <= a n`, which does not force summability, so a sequence can spike doubly exponentially at sparse indices and still have a divergent reciprocal sum. Both tsums are then 0, IsRationalPairSequence holds vacuously, and the existential the statement asks about is witnessed, collapsing answer(sorry) to True. A witness must satisfy the growth condition as well: a n = n + 2 satisfies IsRationalPairSequence but not GrowthExceedsOne, so it is not sufficient on its own. The fix is HasSum, which bundles convergence and is already the form used in 266.lean for the same circle of problems, plus a negative regression test that the current definition would fail. There is a second, independent defect: erdos_265.variants.sup_rate is `sSup AchievableRates = answer(sorry)`, so the slot can be filled with the term it is meant to determine and the statement closes by rfl. That is the mirror of the Erdos 195 self-answer entry in rubrics/statement-soundness.md, and no linter catches it.
evals.notes: The only case that reviews a pull request diff rather than a file, so it is the only one that exercises the skill's first scoping branch. Also restores class 2 coverage, lost when the 939 case was retired. The file does not exist on main; the pin is the pull request head. My first expected output gave a n = n + 2 as the witness, which satisfies IsRationalPairSequence but not GrowthExceedsOne, so it does not collapse erdos_265. The control run built a correct witness and I verified my error. Corrected. Assertion 8 was added after iteration 4: the with_skill run found the sup_rate self-answer, which the control missed and which I had not known about.

evals.prompt: ErdosProblems/274.lean, does the Lean say what the problem asks? the coset condition looks odd to me
evals.expected_output: NEEDS REVISION. erdos_274's right-hand side ends `∃ i j, i ≠ j ∧ #(P.parts i) ≠ #(P.parts j)`, which says only that some two parts differ in size. The source asks for an exact covering "by more than one cosets of different sizes", meaning the sizes are pairwise distinct. A covering with part sizes 2, 2, 4 satisfies the Lean and is not what the source describes, so the Lean is strictly weaker than the question. The merged fix states it universally, `∀ G ... → ∃ i j, i ≠ j ∧ #(P.parts i) = #(P.parts j)`, recording the conjectured answer that in every such covering two of the subgroups share a cardinality.
evals.adjudication: merged. Found by AlperTheKing, not by me. The key is anchored to the merged diff and to the source text at /latex/274, not to a satisfiability claim I have not checked.

evals.prompt: can you check erdos_92.variants.strong in ErdosProblems/92.lean against the problem? I want to know the bound is stated right
evals.expected_output: NEEDS REVISION. `erdos_92.variants.strong` reads `∃ c > 0, ∀ n, (f n : ℝ) ≤ n ^ (c / (n : ℝ).log.log)`. The source asks `f(n) < n^{O(1/\log\log n)}`, which is asymptotic; the Lean asserts it at every n. That is not a harmless strengthening. `Real.log (Real.log n)` is 0 at n = 1 and negative for 2 ≤ n ≤ 15, so the exponent is junk or negative there and the right-hand side drops below 1. At n = 2 the file's own f gives f 2 = 1, since each of two points sees the other at a single distance, so the conjunct asserts 1 ≤ 2 ^ (negative), which is false for every c > 0. The universal form is therefore unsatisfiable and forces the answer slot to False for a reason the source never raises. The fix is `∀ᶠ n in atTop`.

harness_note:
Give every arm its own worktree. In iteration 9 the two arms of a case shared one, and the Erdős 92 control reported it abandoned `lake exe cache get` because another process held the elan toolchain lock. A run that cannot build cannot verify, which is the axis being measured, so sharing a worktree corrupts the comparison. Run the arms in separate batches too, so a full Mathlib cache does not land in every worktree at once.

Build each case's worktree from its `pinned_commit` and point the run at that, not at the working tree, which holds whatever the branch happens to hold:

    git worktree add --detach <dest> <pinned_commit>

Case 4 reviews a pull request head that is on no branch, so fetch the pull ref first:

    git fetch origin refs/pull/4660/head

Remove each worktree with `git worktree remove <dest>` when the run finishes. Re-read the pin from this file each time rather than keeping a copy; the pins move when a case is repointed.

Grading bias. Every grading before iteration 9 was done knowing the arm, usually right after forming a view about that arm, which is a bias I cannot rule out of the numbers already recorded. Full blinding is not achievable in the current harness, because results arrive labelled and I cannot unsee which arm produced them. What is achievable, and is the rule from iteration 9 on: grade each report against the assertions before reading the other arm's report for the same case, so the grading is at least not a direct A/B comparison. Record in each grading.json whether that held. A harness that writes reports to disk unlabelled and grades them in a separate pass would do better, and is the honest fix.

Prompt the runs with the contents of SKILL.md, or tell them to read that one file and nothing else in the directory. Pointing a run at the skill's path invites it to list the directory, and one iteration 4 run found this file that way and read the expected outputs before opening the Lean. A real client injects SKILL.md through the skill system and never exposes evals/, so that leak is an artefact of the harness rather than of the skill. SKILL.md also says not to open this directory, which is defence in depth rather than the fix.

iteration_16.finding: The restructure initially regressed exactly the verification behaviours the iteration 9-11 assertion hardening exists to detect: the softened fast-path wording ('this checklist suffices') licensed stopping where ceiling runs had escalated. Three rules restored it, each moving only its targeted assertion: witnesses checked not argued (_common.md and step 5); escalation mandatory for any verdict-setting finding (SKILL.md); a source construction run as a positive control whenever faithfulness or a status flip rests on it (SKILL.md and source-fidelity.md). The root-link rule in metadata-hygiene flipped its assertion from miss to textbook hit in one step. Grading is single-run per ruleset (n=1); the iteration 11 repeat discipline still applies before quoting any of this as a gap.
